title: The gnome and the formations: he was being cut in half
question: The fix is already in. Does anything in the 'after' sheet still read wrong to you — particularly the width-8 row, where he vanishes completely behind the pillar?
context_md:
Not blind and not a choice — you are seeing a fixed bug, and the only
question I actually need your eye on is the last paragraph.

Rows are formation widths 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. Across a row the stone slides
past him a cell at a time. Both sheets are the real renderer.

**Before** (26 of 46 tiles): look at rows 3, 5 and 8 — he is cut down the
middle, some of his columns drawn over the stone and the rest hidden
behind it. The depth key was the world *column*, and the hash that decides
front-or-behind is built to disagree between neighbouring columns, so a
formation three or more cells wide never agreed with itself. Measured: 0%
of formations put him wholly on one side, from width 3 up.

This was invisible until now only because speleothems are one pixel wide,
which is the thing being replaced tonight — the respec makes them 3-8
cells at the base. So every formation of the new kind would have shipped
him shredded, and at play zoom that reads as sprite detail rather than as
a bug.

**After**: wholly in front, or wholly hidden. 0 of 46.

**What I want your eye on:** in the width-8 row, when he is behind the
pillar he is *gone* — completely invisible. That is your own earlier
ruling ("behind has too much transparency, the player character should be
hidden"), but you made it about trees, and foliage has gaps a solid stone
column does not. A tapered formation is only 8 wide down at his boots, so
he should rarely disappear whole. Tell me if that trade is wrong and I
will give scenery its own alpha rather than sharing the trees'.
